title: Section 205 — Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent

content.overview: BNS s. 205 — Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent. BNS restatement of IPC 171. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 171. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 205 is the rule on “Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent”. The section provides that whoever, not belonging to a certain class of public servants, wears any garb or carries any token resembling any garb or token used by that class of public servants, with the intention that it may be believed, or with the knowledge that it is likely to be believed, that he belongs to that class of public servants, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 205 exists so that “Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent” has a closed legal test in Chapter XII — Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Disobedience, unlawful trade, personation — and a new duty to treat a victim.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 205 constitutes a key component of Chapter XII (Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent under Section 205 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 205.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 205 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 205 vs General Attempt: Section 205 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 205 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 205 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 205 for conduct relating to wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent.
Rule: Under BNS s. 205, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 205.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 205 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
